# Watching a one-shot run progress while it is still going

`rimsky compose run` streams per-node lifecycle lines as they happen, not
batched at exit. A watcher sees which work has settled and which is still
outstanding.

## The manifest

Two instances: one settles immediately, one waits on a slow upstream.

```yaml
project: live-demo
templates:
  - path: ./template-success.yml
    tag: fast
    state: deployed
  - path: ./template-slow.yml
    tag: slow
    state: deployed
instances:
  - template: fast
    name: quick
  - template: slow
    name: lagging
```

`template-slow.yml`:

```yaml
name: slow-http-fetch
version: "1"
message_queue_mode: backlog
nodes:
  - type: fetch
    executor: http-node
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url:
            type: string
            default: http://127.0.0.1:18777/
```

`template-success.yml`:

```yaml
name: shape-checks-pass
version: "1"
message_queue_mode: backlog
nodes:
  - type: verify
    executor: verifier-shape-checks
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          checks:
            type: array
            default:
              - kind: no_nulls
                config:
                  fields: [id]
                severity: error
          rows:
            type: array
            default:
              - id: 1
```

## Run it

```bash
rimsky compose run -f rimsky-compose.yml
```

## What the operator sees

With the slow upstream sleeping eight seconds, the progress stream arrives
spread across the run:

```
+0s  instance live-demo/lagging: tracking
+0s  instance live-demo/quick: tracking
+1s  instance live-demo/lagging node ...: success (terminal/success)
+1s  instance live-demo/quick node ...: success (terminal/success)
+1s  instance live-demo/quick node ...: success (terminal/success)
+2s  instance live-demo/quick: success (nodes=2)
+11s instance live-demo/lagging node ...: success (terminal/success)
+11s instance live-demo/lagging: success (nodes=2)
+11s compose run: all-success (2 instances)
```

The quick instance's per-node outcome is on screen at one second and its
instance summary at two — nine seconds before the command returns, while the
lagging fetch is still outstanding. The lagging instance's lines arrive when
that work actually finishes.

A watcher knows at any moment which work has settled and which is still running.
